class: Reading a file through a remote shell command (ssh host 'type file', 'cat' in a PowerShell default shell, Get-Content) returns the shell's re-encoded text, not the file's bytes - the byte-order mark is dropped, line endings are converted and non-ASCII characters are replaced by the console code page; editing that text and writing it back silently rewrites every such line.
mechanism: Syncing two keys of GLOBAL.env to the Windows VPS: the script read the file with `ssh ... type C:\Abhay\GLOBAL.env` (default shell PowerShell), replaced the two key lines and uploaded the result; the file lost its BOM, went LF -> CRLF and 30 comment lines changed (17,470 -> 16,733 bytes). The script's own check 'uploaded == read back: False' exposed it.

first_seen.evidence: scp byte compare: backup bom True, lone LF 214, 17470 bytes; after the edit bom False, CRLF 214, 16733 bytes, 30 comment lines + the 2 keys differing

fix: Move files with scp (byte-exact) in both directions, edit the bytes, and verify by downloading again with scp and comparing to the intended bytes plus a line diff against a backup taken first. Repaired: the VPS file now equals the backup except the two key lines (BOM and LF kept), proven by scp read-back.

detection.note: Every remote-file edit script ends with an scp read-back equality check and a line diff against a backup taken before the edit; a read-back mismatch stops the run before anything else touches the file.

occurrences.where: GLOBAL.env sync to the Windows VPS
occurrences.evidence: damage caught by the read-back check and repaired from the backup the same turn
